answer: Copycat keys stay cheap unless each new reviewer seat is earned with a photographed crane shift. The harbor posts one 17-hour window on a public jetty crane. The applicant clips a carved ivory tally to the boom, then walks the staked meadow fence while two clerks photograph the tally and three posts at hours 2, 9, and 17. Peers match those frames to the published post map and tally serial. Cost is 17 hours plus a scarce carving a second persona cannot reuse. Shared lot codes, or frames more than 55 seconds off the posted clock, slash bonds 27 percent and freeze crane bookings for eight epochs.
